reason: I'd probably start the free 14-day comparison since there's no auto-charge, and fading volume with earphones in actually suits my lab hours. But I make almost nothing, and YouTube sleep music already works fine for me, so I don't see myself paying 4,900 won a month or 39,000 won up front on top of the subscriptions I already have.
objection: YouTube is free and already puts me to sleep. Saving a few minutes falling asleep isn't worth another monthly charge, and I'm not sure phone-movement tracking even works when my phone is just lying on the bed and I'm wearing earphones in a shared room.
would_change_my_mind: If the 14-day report showed a big, obvious gap, like falling asleep 15+ minutes faster or getting back to sleep much quicker after waking at night, and it cost around 2,000 won a month or there was a student price.
